meta_title: Middle-earth world — peoples, places and history
description: An overview of Middle-earth lore for The Lord of the Rings event: peoples, kingdoms, armies, timeline, geography and thematic lore for players and newcomers.
title: Middle-earth world
subtitle: Lore, peoples, places and the history of the world in which our game takes place.
intro: The Lord of the Rings is set in a world inspired by Tolkien’s Middle-earth. This part of the website helps you understand the wider historical, cultural and geographic background — who you’ll meet in the game, who has scores with whom, where they come from, what you wear and what you talk about in camp.

h_what: What you’ll find in this section

kanon_p: Some parts of our lore content go hand in hand with Tolkien’s books. Others are our interpretation — for the needs of the game, the year’s story or the dramaturgy of a specific weekend. In the texts we use tags so it’s clear what is what:
tag1_desc: In line with the books and appendices.
tag2_desc: Our LARP interpretation — doesn’t have to fit the canon literally.
tag3_desc: Helps with the costume and atmosphere.
tag5_desc: Doesn’t change game rules; it’s the lore layer.

h_year: How Middle-earth maps to our year
year_p1: The Lord of the Rings is a LARP interpretation of Tolkien’s world. We start from the atmosphere, peoples and main conflicts, but we keep the freedom for our own story and our own decisions of characters. It is not a literal transfer of the books or the film — it is a weekend in which players share a world together and create another part of its story.

cta_p: Enjoying the lore? Have a look at the practical information about the armies — what the costume looks like, what the combat style is, who the army suits and how to sign up.
footer_note: This part of the website serves as a fan and game guide. It is not an official encyclopaedia of Tolkien’s work. We write the texts in our own words, without direct quotations from the books, the film or wikis.
